chapter: New York, Henderson and Charlie Johnson
title: Leaving Henderson when the pay turned bad
summary: He worked with Henderson only once, was proud of playing the book unrehearsed, and left when Fletcher announced a pay cut, recognizing the signs from his carnival days.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: : Was -- while you were with Fletcher -- you were with Fletcher several times, weren't you? A couple of times?

No, that was it. I went in and I played first trumpet after what's-his-name, and I was proud of it, and I stick my chest up because I was able to go in there and play that book without a rehearsal, and he was happy, I was happy, so that makes me feel doggone good. Okay?
: What sort of a relationship did you have with Fletcher?

With Fletcher? Well, I mean playing his music, everything was fine. And (Laughs) til he got to the other part, where I came in, I told you I was with carnivals, and road shows, and I knew I was with the greatest con men in the world, you know? So when he said well folks, we're going to Philadelphia, the scales and so-and-so, I can't play with so, I said Good-bye! And that was it, you know.
But I would -- I said -- and I thanked him very much, and I split, because I knew the end of the
story, and I went through that when I first came into show business, you know.
So you know when to get off --
Oh man, I know -- I mean I knew when to run out, you know. (Laughs.)
